readout_other: Progressive-ratio and FR3 operant responding for oral fentanyl/sucrose; MR-ARFI displacement at the focus
direction_notes: MRgLIFU of bilateral NAc under three sonication schemes did not change progressive-ratio responding for fentanyl/sucrose at 4 or 24 h, versus anesthesia-only controls.

device.model: MR-compatible 1.5 MHz FUS system, 8-element annular array

timing.protocol_description: Scheme 1: 500 ms bursts repeated every 5000 ms, containing 5 ms pulses at 100 Hz, for 15 min at 2.0 MPa. Schemes 2 and 3: 300 ms pulses at 1 Hz (30% duty cycle) with no burst structure, for 10 or 20 min at 0.9 MPa. Repeated rounds, up to three per rat, one week or more apart.

source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.duty_cycle_pct: In this study, we employed three sonication schemes to investigate their impact on fentanyl motivation: a Burst Mode (Scheme 1), utilizing 500 ms bursts of sub-pulses (50% duty cycle, 100 Hz PRF) delivered every 5 seconds, a Continuous Mode (Scheme 2), consisting of 300 ms pulses at a 1 Hz repetition frequency for 10 min., and a similar but longer Continuous Mode using 20 min. sonication duration (Scheme 3).
